changed since I last looked at this).

### Description

When I register using OpenID everything works perfectly until I get the activation email, which leads me to the form which requires a password. At this moment I cannot insert any password (because my account is not properly activated), and I don't even get a button for resetting the password.

gitea.com today

Firefox 127

body: Apparently this is still a problem, even in downstream forks (Forgejo  Version: 13.0.1)

> Apparently this is still a problem, even in downstream forks (Forgejo Version: 13.0.1)

By the way, Forgejo is not really a fork now, they don't follow Gitea's code. Many features are Gitea-only.

> > Apparently this is still a problem, even in downstream forks (Forgejo Version: 13.0.1)
> 
> By the way, Forgejo is not really a fork now, they don't follow Gitea's code. Many features are Gitea-only.

Well, it is what I would call hostile fork, the one which not only doesn’t expect to merge, but makes conspicuous changes to make cooperation impossible (e.g., by changing the license): https://blog.codeberg.org/codeberg-launches-forgejo.html

A user may not have a local password at all, since cloning/pulling/pushing can be done using a PAT. Because user.IsPasswordSet already indicates whether a password exists, I’m not sure why a password is now required. I couldn’t find any reason that a local password must be enforced. Even if a user cannot log in via OpenID, an administrator can still set a local password using the admin console command.
